title: Withdraw a tightly shelved book by exposing both covers
instruction: Ease the tan books back to make room on both sides of the blue book. Grasp both covers near the middle of its spine before easing it out. Protect the top of the spine from hooking or pressure. Lay the closed book flat, fully on the mat, and move both hands clear. Leave both tan books standing securely in the bay.
context: A reader choosing a book from a crowded shelf at home, at school or in a library may have too little room above it to reach the far edge. Sliding the neighbouring books back exposes both covers so the reader can draw out the chosen book without hooking the fragile top of its spine, then lay it flat for use.
setup: The blue book stands between two tan books. Each is 125 mm deep, 30 mm thick and 180 mm high. The bay has 165 mm of usable depth, 94 mm of width and 188 mm of height above its floor. The landing mat is 170 mm front to back and 220 mm across. Its centre is 140 mm ahead of the shelf lip and its top is 15 mm below the shelf floor.
scoring: For a real trial, use synchronized close-ups of both pad-to-cover interfaces and an overview with a millimetre scale at the shelf lip. Film from the flush start through release and hand withdrawal until all finish conditions have held for two uninterrupted seconds or the 60-second limit expires. Award the highest verified level, subject to the whole-trial failures below. Score 0 if no level is reached. Score 0.25 when both tan spines are behind the lip and expose the blue cover bands on both sides before withdrawal. Score 0.50 when opposite pads of one gripper visibly touch those bands before the first outward pull and stay seated as the spine moves 3 mm out from its furthest inward position. After a valid first pull, score 0.75 when all blue book corners are in front of the lip and the book is held or resting on a support surface. A change of grip after the 3 mm crossing is allowed. Score 1.0 for a valid first pull followed by two uninterrupted seconds with a broad cover resting flat on the mat without overhang, both tan books upright inside the bay on their bottom edges, all three books still and both hands clear. Score the neighbours' stability during that final dwell. Visible hooking, pressing or pulling on the marked headcap by either arm at any time, or failure of the exposure or grasp check on the first 3 mm pull, overrides all credit with 0. If the footage cannot resolve a required safety check, record the trial as unscorable. The README gives the spatial bounds and frame checks.
reset_notes: Place all three books on their bottom edges with the spines facing out. Align the spines with the bay lip using a removable straightedge. Use 1 mm shims for both book-to-book gaps and both outer gaps. Remove the gauges, check independent sliding, restore alignment and start from the standard robot reset.
fidelity: Closed rigid books preserve the access problem. The two lighter blue regions are solid parts of the cover boards that register contact. A separate solid piece at the upper spine registers headcap load. The task measures where the withdrawal load is applied and how the book comes to rest. It does not estimate damage to a binding.
